Participants face no retrospective sanctions and can choose whether to speak to the forum.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Cricket Australia broadened its independent inquiry regarding ball-tampering to also examine the Ashes series played in 2017-18. This followed claims made in a book by a former player suggesting the whole team knew about the tampering during a tour to South Africa. While some former team members supported these claims, current and other past players denied them.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The renewed focus brings fresh attention to a major past cricket scandal. The governing body stated that the inquiry provides a safe environment for participants to share accounts, while ensuring no retroactive punishments will occur.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The independent forum will remain open for six weeks, inviting past players, support staff, and management to contribute. A full report containing recommendations will be published within thirty days after the board receives it.

gist: New Zealand defeated England twenty six to eight in rainy Twickenham.
The visitors adapted better to the wet conditions than the hosts.
England suffered from poor discipline and conceded two yellow cards.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: New Zealand bounced back from their previous defeat by beating England twenty six to eight in heavy rain. Wallace Sititi and Cam Roigard scored tries for the visitors, while Richie Mo'unga kicked four penalties and two conversions. Henry Slade kicked an early penalty for England, and Jamie George scored a late try.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: England's discipline collapsed under scoreboard pressure, resulting in yellow cards for Alex Coles and Henry Pollock. The defeat provides valuable lessons for Steve Borthwick's side ahead of their upcoming Six Nations campaign.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Ireland defeated Australia 38-14 in London to finish the year with four consecutive autumn wins. Australia took an early lead through a try by Jeremy Williams. Kalani Thomas scored for Australia, before replacement James McNabney added two late tries.

gist: The All Blacks face a rare decline in form and financial stability.
Financial struggles threaten New Zealand Rugby's ability to keep top players at home.
Growing departures of mid-career stars and reliance on tradition present ongoing challenges.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The All Blacks have suffered a downturn, on course for their least successful decade since the 1970s and facing a potential sixth defeat of the calendar year. Financially, New Zealand Rugby faces projected multi-million-pound losses, leading to the departure of star players to overseas clubs in France and Japan.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Financial pressures and the loss of mid-career talent threaten the team's global dominance and historic legacy. While traditional coaching methods and domestic eligibility rules once protected the All Blacks, rising costs and competitive overseas salaries make it harder to retain top players.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The All Blacks prepare to play England at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham aiming to avoid another defeat as New Zealand Rugby navigates a challenging long-term financial and strategic future.
